identity.name: Disodium inosinate
identity.chemical_class: Purine nucleotide salt (disodium salt of inosinic acid)

function.mechanism: Enhances umami signaling and synergizes with glutamate systems, increasing savory intensity and perceived saltiness at comparable sodium levels.

adi.basis: EFSA 2025 established a group ADI of 2.7 mg inosinic acid/kg bw/day for E630 and E631 (converted from 5 mg inosinic + guanylic acids/kg bw/day by molecular-weight adjustment).

efsa.key_finding: EFSA concluded exposure estimates did not exceed group ADIs in any assessed population group and scenario at reported use levels.

fda.notes: Direct food additive permitted as flavoring adjuvant with compositional conditions; no explicit disodium inosinate entry found in retrieved 21 CFR parts 182 or 184 GRAS text.

adi.basis: JECFA database lists ADI as NOT SPECIFIED for disodium 5'-inosinate in a group context with inosinic acid and salts.

concerns.summary: IMP is a purine nucleotide; clinical dosing studies show it can raise serum uric acid, indicating a plausible risk pathway for hyperuricemia-prone individuals at high exposures.
In feed-additive assessments, EFSA FEEDAP initially flagged unresolved production-strain safety uncertainties (2022) that were later resolved with supplementary data (2023).

no_concern_confirmed: EFSA 2025 re-evaluation reported no group-ADI exceedance in assessed populations/scenarios at reported use levels.
JECFA entry reports ADI not specified for disodium 5'-inosinate group context.
EFSA FEEDAP 2023 concluded IMP from C. stationis KCCM 80235 was safe for target species, consumers, users and the environment in assessed feed context.

adi_exceedance.notes: EFSA 2025 reported no exceedance of established group ADIs across assessed population groups and scenarios.

risk_assessment.rationale: E631 is authorized in major jurisdictions reviewed, has explicit U.S. use conditions, and EFSA's 2025 re-evaluation found no group-ADI exceedance at reported uses. Available concern signals are mainly mechanistic/high-dose purine-uric-acid considerations rather than demonstrated population-level harm at current additive exposures.
key_factors: EFSA 2025 established group ADIs and reported no exceedance in assessed populations
21 CFR 172.535 permits disodium inosinate with defined conditions
JECFA lists ADI as not specified in group context
No IARC classification entry found for disodium inosinate
Clinical IMP data show uric-acid elevation potential at therapeutic dosing
